gloss: June (traditional name); a type of wagashi

definitions.explanation: The old Japanese name for the sixth month. Despite the characters literally suggesting 'month without water,' it actually refers to the month when rice paddies are filled with water ({水|みず}の{月|つき}). Still used in literary, poetic, and cultural contexts.

definitions.gloss: a triangular wagashi (Japanese sweet) eaten on June 30
definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese confection made of sweetened rice flour topped with sweet azuki beans. It has a distinctive triangular shape representing ice. Eaten on June 30 as part of the Nagoshi no Harae purification ritual to ward off illness for the rest of the year.

notes:
One of the twelve traditional Japanese month names ({和風月名|わふうげつめい}). The characters {水|みず}{無|な}{月|つき} literally mean "month without water," but this is interpreted as ⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{月|つき}→月：02230_tsuki⟧ (month of water), referring to the flooding of rice paddies during the rainy season.

TRADITIONAL MONTH NAMES:
- ⟦{睦月|むつき}→睦月：18674_mutsuki⟧ (January), ⟦{如月|きさらぎ}→如月：20361_kisaragi⟧ (February), ⟦{弥生|やよい}→弥生：20353_yayoi⟧ (March)
- {卯月|うづき} (April), {皐月|さつき} (May), {水無月|みなづき} (June)
- {文月|ふみづき} (July), ⟦{葉月|はづき}→葉月：22859_hazuki⟧ (August), {長月|ながつき} (September)

CULTURAL NOTE:
The {水無月|みなづき} sweet (sense 2) is especially associated with ⟦{京都|きょうと}→京都：09484_kyouto⟧. It is eaten on June 30 during {夏越|なごし}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{祓|はら}え→祓う：13897_harau⟧, a Shinto purification ritual held at the midpoint of the year. The triangular shape symbolizes ice, which was a luxury in ancient times, and eating it was believed to ward off summer illness.
